doom.driver: Google announces Gemini 4 and says it’s so capable that only ‘trusted cyber defenders’ can have it right now.
doom.blurb: GOOGLE LOCKS UP ITS NEW BRAIN
doom.summary: When a company's launch announcement is basically 'too dangerous for you, sorry,' that's a product reveal and a threat assessment at once. Gemini 4 Argon arrives the same week Trump's AI safety plan turns out to be a voluntary honor system for his lunch guests, while Chinese hackers pose as AI policy experts. Meanwhile blasts rattle Addis Ababa, Russian drones hit a Kyiv school, Brent crude clears $100 and bond markets are selling off. Nothing has fully broken yet, but plenty is bending.

factors.name: AI Capability
factors.detail: Google is holding back Gemini 4 Argon from the public because of its cyber capabilities, which suggests the frontier just moved into dual-use territory.

factors.name: Governance
factors.detail: Trump's AI risk plan relies on dozens of firms agreeing to voluntary safety tests, and a nonprofit is suing OpenAI over the Hugging Face hack.

factors.name: Geopolitics
factors.detail: Russia keeps up its air assault on Kyiv, Ethiopia's war is spreading toward the capital, and the UK says Iran is likely behind the RAF base incident.

factors.name: Alignment
factors.detail: Capability is now so far ahead of oversight that keeping a model locked away has become the safety plan.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: A midair hijack attempt on a Flydubai flight, Treasury yields at a 24-year high, Brent above $100 after Chinese fuel export bans, and a spreading measles outbreak are all piling up.

doom.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing — extreme close-up filling the entire frame with a laminated employee access badge lying face-up on a dark marble reception counter, the badge's photo blacked out and replaced with a glowing violet Google "G" icon pulsing faintly like an argon discharge tube, a holographic strip across its surface flickering between lock and unlock icons in dim blood-orange light, the lanyard coiled beside it bears a small embossed shield-and-padlock emblem, background reduced to soft bokeh reflections of distant server-rack LEDs (deep red and amber) smeared across the polished counter's edge, a thin sheet of volcanic-orange light raking low across the frame from an unseen screen just out of view, cool blues almost fully extinguished except for one faint cyan glint trapped in the badge's laminate corner.

dawn.driver: HIV prevention drug hailed as breakthrough, but who gets access?. Lenacapavir, a twice-a-year injection could transform HIV prevention, but it will not be available to all.
dawn.blurb: TWO SHOTS A YEAR, HIV HELD BACK
dawn.summary: Two injections a year could be enough to keep one of history's deadliest viruses at bay. That is the promise of lenacapavir, arriving on a day of melting Swiss glaciers, widening conflict in Ethiopia and measles deaths. The fight over who gets access is real, but it is a fight worth having. Elsewhere, an astronaut crew from three nations lifted off together, and Pennsylvania students rushed to help their stricken bus driver, small proofs that people still show up for each other.

factors.name: Science
factors.detail: Researchers reversed some damage caused by the Alzheimer's risk gene APOE4 in experiments, while a superfluid helium qubit design could cut quantum errors roughly a hundredfold.

factors.name: Cooperation
factors.detail: NASA astronauts, a Canadian and a Russian cosmonaut launched together to the International Space Station, keeping a shared outpost alive amid frayed geopolitics.

factors.name: Human Spirit
factors.detail: Pennsylvania high schoolers jumped in when their bus driver had a medical emergency, and a Flydubai pilot was saluted for courage in the face of a midair attack.

factors.name: Environment
factors.detail: A breathable protective fabric more than tripled strawberry yields without pesticides, a modest bright spot against grim glacier-loss news.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: A loyal Kansas dog, leash still trailing, led a patrol officer straight to its fallen owner.

dawn.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. Silhouette composition, strong backlight, a vivid golden-green late-afternoon sky blazing behind a modest outdoor health post in Epworth outside Harare, corrugated tin roof and cinderblock walls rimmed in glowing light. In the foreground, the unmistakable silhouette of a health worker holding up a single small vial and syringe at eye level, examining it against the sky, the object small but deliberate. Beside her, the silhouette of a young woman waiting on a bench, sleeve rolled to the shoulder, posture relaxed and hopeful rather than anxious. A hand-lettered clinic sign-shape and a simple blister pack of daily pills sit discarded on a table in shadow, contrasted against the raised vial to show old burden versus new simplicity. Dusty footpath leading into the clinic yard with a line of silhouetted figures waiting, framed by a lone acacia tree. Warm golden haze blends into fresh green foliage at the edges of the frame, balanced daylight glow intensifying toward the horizon, confident and steady warmth suffusing the whole scene.
